behaviours.description: Periodic entry point: initialises the device, consumes a CAN-supplied time, and runs the low-voltage check and the time adjustment at their own configured intervals measured against the OS tick.
Brings up the real-time clock device over the shared I2C interface, configuring the prescaler and control register through the module's write buffer.
Consumes a time-of-day message received over CAN and applies it to the device when one is present.
Compares the device's time against the system timer and re-initialises the system time from the device once the two differ by more than the configured maximum difference.
Reads the device's battery-low voltage alert flag and reports it, which is the RTC's own supply monitoring rather than a pack measurement.
The two module-scope transfer buffers shared by every I2C access this driver makes; their sharing is what deviation FB2-SW-DEV-000014 records.

concurrency_and_isr_context.shared_state: The module-scope I2C buffers rtc_i2cWriteBuffer and rtc_i2cReadBuffer, and the module's own time state. The buffers are shared by every transfer the driver makes, which is safe only while all callers are in one task; the record states that this is a single-context module rather than asserting a protection the code does not visibly implement.

limitations: IMPORTANT: rtc.c differs between the pinned commit and the current working tree. The working-tree file has 14 lines added inside RTC_AdjustTime relative to the pin, so every line_range in this record is a PINNED-commit range and will not match the checked-out file line-for-line. The content_hash recorded is the pinned blob's, deliberately, because the record's commit field says 308028fb and a hash of different bytes under that commit label would be a false statement. A reader diffing these ranges against the working tree will find RTC_AdjustTime spanning 252-289 rather than 252-276; the added lines are a replacement of an abs() call on a time_t difference with a signed two-sided comparison.

The source-registry anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000044 and -000045 record the same pinned hash this record does, so the provenance validator's reported mismatch on those two anchors is a worktree-drift report and not a disagreement about what was read.
Behaviour was verified by reading the code. No real-time clock device was present, no time source was synchronised, and no drift measurement exists in this corpus.

The RTC register addresses, bit masks and the two module-scope buffer sizes are device-specific values whose authoritative definition is the device header; they are named but their values are not restated here, so this record cannot become a second unverifiable copy of the device's register map.
evidence_status.method: rtc.c was read at the pinned commit with 'git show 308028fb:src/app/driver/rtc/rtc.c'; the content_hash recorded is that pinned blob's sha256, which is the value anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000044 and -000045 already carry. Each named symbol was confirmed to occur inside its recorded line_range at the pin and each range was confirmed within the file. The function spans were determined from the pinned content directly.

guard.statement: This record says where the RTC driver code is and what it does. It implements no design artefact and realises no requirement in this profile, and both gaps are declared. It is not evidence that any requirement is met, and no time source, clock drift or synchronisation behaviour was measured. It confers no production authority, no verification credit and no human approval.

implements.design_gap_reason: The as_is profile contains no software design artefact for the RTC driver. Its three design records cover the AFE driver, the SOA module and the contactor driver, and deviations FB2-SW-DEV-000014 and -000015 each record rtc.c as gap_no_design_artifact_in_profile. Attaching this module to an existing design would assert timekeeping design coverage the profile does not have, so design_artifact_id is null and no implements link is created. This is a typed leaf exception under master prompt section 13.
implements.relationship: No design artefact in the as_is profile describes the RTC driver, so there is no design for this element to implement and no implements link is asserted. What the module does, read from the pinned source: RTC_Trigger (rtc.c:420-445) is the periodic entry point. It calls RTC_Initialize, and only if that returns STD_OK does it proceed: it then calls RTC_SetOverCanMessage to consume a time received over CAN, and it gates two periodic activities on elapsed OS ticks measured against RTC_TIME_BETWEEN_BATTERY_LOW_FLAG_CHECK_min and RTC_TIME_BETWEEN_RTC_TIMER_ADJUSTMENT_min, each scaled by RTC_FACTOR_MIN_TO_MS. RTC_Initialize (447-590) brings up the device over the shared I2C interface, which is where the two module-scope buffers rtc_i2cWriteBuffer and rtc_i2cReadBuffer (80-82) that anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000045 records come in; deviation FB2-SW-DEV-000015 records the sharing of those buffers. RTC_AdjustTime (252-276) compares the device's time against the system timer and re-initialises the system time from the device when they differ by more than RTC_MAX_DIFFERENCE_BETWEEN_TIMER_AND_IC_s. RTC_CheckBatteryLowVoltageAlert (278-310) reads the device's voltage-alert flag. So the driver provides device access, periodic scheduling against the OS tick, and reconciliation of an external time source against the internal one.

required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
